subject: physics
title: Electric fields
key_idea: A charged object creates an **electric field** around it. Another charged object in the field feels a force. The field is strongest close to the charge. Fields explain the non-contact force between charges and sparking.

blocks.text: A charged object creates an electric field around itself. This section covers what the field is and how its strength changes.

items.meaning: The region around a charged object where another charged object experiences a force.

items: The electric field is strongest close to the charged object.
The further away from the charged object, the weaker the field.
A second charged object placed in the field experiences a force.
The force gets stronger as the distance between the objects decreases.
Sphere A has an electric field, and sphere B is in it.
So sphere B experiences a force without touching sphere A.
The force can be attraction or repulsion, depending on the charges.

blocks.text: In the alpha particle scattering experiment, a positive alpha particle approaching a positive gold nucleus is repelled. The field strength and the force on it increase as it gets closer.

items: An electric field is the region where a charged object experiences a force.
The field is stronger closer to the charge, and so is the force.
A charged object in the field of another feels a force without contact.

blocks.text: Field lines show the shape, the direction and the strength of an electric field.

items: The arrows show the direction of the force on a positive charge.
Lines that are close together show a strong field.
Lines that are far apart show a weak field.

diagram.alt: Two electric field patterns compared: an isolated charged sphere and parallel plates.
items: Isolated charged sphere
Between parallel plates

values: Straight lines that point directly towards or away from the sphere.
Straight, parallel and equally spaced lines.
Away from a positive sphere. Towards a negative sphere.
From the positive plate to the negative plate.
Strongest close to the sphere, where the lines are closest together.
The same everywhere between the plates (away from the edges), because the lines are equally spaced.

blocks.text: An electric field pattern is similar to a magnetic field pattern. Closeness of the lines shows strength, and both show the direction of the force.

items: Field lines for an isolated sphere are straight and radial, away from positive and towards negative.
Between parallel plates the lines are parallel and equally spaced.
Closer lines mean a stronger field.

blocks.text: Electric fields also explain sparks. A very strong field can make air conduct.

diagram.alt: Put the steps that lead to a spark between a charged object and an earthed conductor into order.
steps: A charged object is brought close to an earthed conductor.
The electric field strength between them becomes very high.
The air becomes ionised, so it conducts.
Charge flows through the air and a spark jumps.

items: Air is normally an insulator with a high resistance.
In a very strong field the air breaks down and becomes ionised.
The ionised air conducts, so electrons move across the gap as a spark.
A kite flown very close to an overhead power cable can give a fatal shock for this reason. The ionised air, and the kite or string, conduct charge to the person.
A very strong electric field ionises the air.
Ionised air conducts, so charge moves across the gap as a spark.
The object does not need to touch the power cable for a dangerous shock.

checks.a: The region around a charged object where another charged object experiences a force.

checks.q: How does the electric field strength vary as the distance from a charged object increases?
Explain why a spark can jump between a charged rod and an earthed conductor that are close together.
checks.a: The electric field strength is very high, so the air becomes ionised and conducts. Electrons move through the air from the rod to the conductor.

worked_example.question: It is dangerous for a person to fly a kite near an overhead power cable. The person could receive a fatal electric shock if the kite was very close to, but not touching the power cable. Explain why.
answer_points: The electric field strength is very high.
This causes the air to become ionised (the air breaks down or becomes a conductor).
The kite or string conducts charge to the person or to earth.
worked_example.tip: One mark for each step. Do not write about the kite touching the power cable.

worked_example.question: Metal sphere A is fixed to a table. Metal sphere B can be moved. Metal sphere B is placed at a short distance from metal sphere A. Both spheres are insulated from the table and given a negative charge. The force between the charged spheres is measured. Explain, in terms of electric fields, why a force is exerted on sphere B.
answer_points: Sphere A has an electric field.
worked_example.tip: Do not write about the nature of the force, such as repulsion. It is ignored.

worked_example.question: An electrostatic dust precipitator uses static electricity to remove smoke particles from gases before the gases are released from a chimney in a factory. The precipitator uses high voltages. Why are high voltages dangerous?
answer_points: High voltages can cause electric shocks or electrocution.
worked_example.tip: Unqualified answers such as dangerous or heating are ignored. Electrocution, with damage to the nervous system or heart, is also credited.
